correctness.rationale: For an off-spectrum target and a one-site block v0, the resolvent equation is exactly (I+v0 T0)x=0 for a nonzero site vector x. The operator-norm inequality gives the universal lower bound ||v0|| >= 1/||T0||. A largest right singular vector of T0 constructs a block attaining equality, and an orthogonal second singular direction raises the block norm to any prescribed Q above threshold without changing the kernel vector. The resulting resolvent vector is in l2 because lambda is in the free resolvent set. The boundary corollary follows algebraically. The packaged verifier replays representative complex cases and an off-diagonal-dominance obstruction; it is corroborative only.

value.rationale: The source paper uses one-site potentials as its sharpness mechanism but only obtains partial boundary optimality. The new result exactly characterizes the norm budget of that whole natural witness class, proving that outside the diagonal-dominance region the point-potential strategy is impossible at the source boundary norm. This isolates a genuine structural obstruction and shows that any further optimality argument there must use multi-site support or a different mechanism.
